passage: Dr. Amara Chen led a two-year study tracking sleep patterns in over 400 shift workers across six hospitals. The study found that nurses working rotating night shifts reported significantly more trouble falling asleep than those on fixed schedules. Chen's team recommended that hospitals adopt fixed shift schedules whenever possible, and several hospitals in the study began piloting the change within months of the report's publication. The research was funded by a grant from the national health ministry and published in a peer-reviewed sleep medicine journal. Chen said the next phase of research would examine whether the sleep improvements led to fewer medical errors during night shifts.
